title: Psychology
about: A place to watch yourself over time: how the mood moves, what happened, what you noticed. It describes and never diagnoses.

patterns.empty: No mood in this period yet. Mark the mood of a day in the diary — or tap it in the evening message of the bot — and the patterns appear here.
patterns.whatGoesWith: What goes with a good day
patterns.bestDay: The best day of the week
patterns.hardestDay: The hardest day of the week
patterns.byWeekday: By the day of the week
patterns.fewWeeks: A second week with a mood is needed for a line.
patterns.duringEventsHint: The average mood of the days of each event, against the average of the period.

reflection.hint: A few questions about the week, to answer in your own words. With an AI connected they are written from your own week; otherwise three standard ones are asked.
reflection.weekly: Send the questions every Sunday at 18:00
reflection.checkIn: A short evening check-in — the mood in one tap and a few words — is the evening reminder of the Diary: switch it on there.
reflection.byAi: Written from your week by the AI
reflection.empty: No questions yet: press “Questions of this week”.
reflection.confirmDelete: Delete the questions of this week with the answers?

notes.placeholder: What did you notice about yourself?
notes.empty: No notes yet. Write down what you notice: a reaction, a habit, a thought that keeps coming back.

checkups.notDiagnosis: These short questionnaires are a way to watch yourself over time, not a diagnosis. Only a specialist who talks to you can tell what a score means.
checkups.careTitle: You do not have to carry this alone
checkups.careText: One of your answers speaks of thoughts of not wanting to live or of hurting yourself. Such thoughts are a sign of how hard things are, and they deserve attention. Please tell someone you trust, or a doctor or a psychologist. If you feel you may be in danger right now, call your local emergency number or a crisis line.

events.title: What happened
events.toHint: Empty: one day, or still going on
events.birthYearHint: Puts the events told by age in their place among the others
events.empty: No events yet. Write down what happens in your life with its dates — or the age it happened at: a move, an illness, a trip, a new job.
events.exportHint: The events that touch the period — all of them when it is empty — as an Excel workbook or a Word document.

who5.name: WHO-5 well-being
who5.about: Five statements about the last two weeks. The higher the score, the better the well-being.
who5.intro: For each statement choose what is closest to how you have felt over the last two weeks.

items.1: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits
items.2: I have felt calm and relaxed
items.3: I have felt active and vigorous
items.4: I woke up feeling fresh and rested
items.5: My daily life has been filled with things that interest me

answers.2: Less than half of the time
answers.3: More than half of the time

bands.low: Low well-being — worth paying attention to

gad7.name: GAD-7 anxiety
gad7.about: Seven questions about worry over the last two weeks. The lower the score, the calmer.
gad7.intro: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following?

items.1: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge
items.2: Not being able to stop or control worrying
items.3: Worrying too much about different things
items.5: Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
items.7: Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen

bands.moderate: Moderate — worth talking to a specialist
bands.severe: High — worth talking to a specialist

phq9.name: PHQ-9 low mood
phq9.about: Nine questions about mood and energy over the last two weeks. The lower the score, the better.
phq9.intro: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following?

items.1: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
items.3: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
items.4: Feeling tired or having little energy
items.6: Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
items.7: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading or watching television
items.8: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed — or the opposite, being so restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
items.9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way

bands.moderate: Moderate — worth talking to a specialist
bands.moderatelySevere: Quite high — worth talking to a specialist
bands.severe: High — please talk to a specialist
